NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday directed former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal to first surrender within three weeks, saying that his appeal against conviction and 10-year imprisonment in a rape case would be heard only thereafter.Justice Alok Aradhe rejected Tejpal’s plea for exemption from surrendering and asked him to file a surrender certificate before it. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, sought three weeks’ time to surrender, the bench granted him time to surrender.Goa govt opposed his plea for exemption from surrendering and said his appeal was not admissible since he had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.The Goa bench of Bombay HC convicted Tejpal under multiple provisions of Indian Penal Code (IPC) and sentenced him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment each under Sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k), with the sentences to run concurrently.The case relates to two alleged incidents at Grand Hyatt in Goa during Tehelka’s THiNK Fest in Nov 2013. The high court found the victim’s evidence consistent and credible despite extensive cross-examination. The case against Tejpal involves allegations that he sexually assaulted a junior colleague twice in 2013, in an elevator of a high-end hotel in Goa.The Goa Police subsequently registered an FIR against Tarun Tejpal.
Article Summary: Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal to first surrender within three weeks. His appeal against conviction and 10-year imprisonment in a rape case would be heard only thereafter. The case relates to two alleged incidents at Grand Hyatt in Goa in Nov 2013.

Article Title: NMC pushes old doctors to re-register, but can’t net new ones
Article Text:
Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice.

NMC pushes old docs to re-register, but can’t net new ones

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

National Medical Commission (NMC) is seeking to re-register around 11 lakh doctors to create an updated national medical registry, yet it has failed to register even fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sharing records every year, reports Rema Nagarajan.Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice, but only 44,400 entries were recorded in 2025 with at least 24,000 graduates missing in Indian Medical Register. The gap points to potential failure of NMC to sync state and national registries, as required under NMC Act.The National Medical Commission (NMC) is pushing a regulation to make about 11 lakh doctors re-register to create an updated national medical registry, but it has failed to even register fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sending it new entries every year.With over 91,000 MBBS seats available in 2020-21, even with an estimated 75-90% pass percentage, at least 68,000 MBBS graduates should have registered to practice in 2025. Yet the Indian Medical Register shows just over 44,400 entries. That means at least 24,000 of those who graduated just last year are missing from the registry.If thousands of foreign medical graduates who register each year are included, the number of freshly minted doctors missing from the registry would be even more.For instance, in 2023, over 10,000 foreign medical graduates passed the qualifying exam, after which they have to complete a mandatory one-year internship before receiving permanent registration that would make them eligible to practice in India. So, most of these 10,000 would have registered in 2025. Thus, the total number of doctors registering in 2025 would be roughly 80,000, but just over half the number (55%) have been added to the registry.Most of the doctors would have registered with state medical councils. However, new entries in state medical council registries are not being reflected in the national registry as the NMC is yet to synchronise all state registries with the national registry. The NMC Act, 2019, had mandated such synchronisation. It is yet to happen, almost six years after the NMC was constituted in Sept 2020. Neither is NMC adding the new entries that many state councils send every year.Take Assam Medical Council, for instance. It is a state with only govt medical colleges. In the national registry, there are a total of 25,722 registrations from the state council. It shows only one entry for 2025, zero for 2024 and 2023, 106 entries for 2022 and 353 in 2021. The website shows 890 registered in 2024. There were over 720 seats in Assam in 2015 and 1,000 seats in 2020. How is NMC accepting zero entries in 2023 and 2024, or only 106 in 2022?Similarly, NMC’s registry has a total of 67,142 entries from Kerala with just seven entries in 2025 and 17 in 2024. In 2014, Kerala had 3,650 MBBS seats, which increased to 4,500 by 2020. “We are sending details every year... In the name of a new updated NMR, they are not updating the existing one,” said KSMC chief Dr Harikumaran Nair.If the NMC were to register only those who became doctors in the last five years, including foreign medical graduates, it would have had an updated registry of over 3.5 lakh doctors (32%) of the estimated 11 lakh who are said to be available.
Article Summary: Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice. Only 44,400 entries were recorded in 2025 with at least 24,000 graduates missing in Indian Medical Register. The gap points to potential failure of NMC to sync state and national registries.

Article Title: Of 27 lakh ‘logical discrepancy’ deletions in West Bengal, only 7 lakh appealed
Article Text:
This was new information for SC, which was concerned by pendency of 37 lakh appeals

Chunk of WB appeals was against inclusion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a new twist to the simmering controversy over the West Bengal SIR, Supreme Court was informed Tuesday that against 27-lakh odd deletions from voters’ list because of ‘logical discrepancy’ only seven lakh filed appeals seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was informed by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan that of total 38.1 lakh appeals filed before the SIR appellate tribunals, an overwhelming 31 lakh were filed by those who challenged inclusion of names in the rolls claiming they were ineligible to be voters in Bengal.This was new information for SC, which was concerned by pendency of 37 lakh appeals, as 19 tribunals in last four months decided only 82,000 appeals. The new turn means 20 lakh of 27-lakh-odd voters deleted for logical discrepancy have not appealed against being struck off the rolls during the SIR.SC said a chunk of appeals was by those challenging inclusion. EC will give breakup differentiating those seeking inclusion from exclusion. Prioritising inclusion appeals would considerably reduce burden on tribunals, it said.For petitioner Prasenjit Bose from Congress, advocates Gopal Sankaranarayanan and Neha Rathi alleged that bulk of appeals for exclusion/deletion have been filed by EC in a mechanical manner against orders of judicial officers who had directed inclusion of the names and these appeals should not be heard at all.Sankaranarayanan said Kolkata and Howrah civic polls are due in Dec and at least appeals pertaining to these areas should be decided expeditiously so nobody gets disenfranchised illegally.SC said its main concern was expeditious decision on appeals of disenfranchised people. It directed EC to respond with data on appeals pending after segregating them into two categories — those seeking inclusion and those seeking exclusion of names. It asked EC to suggest a mechanism for speeding up disposal, including increasing the number of tribunals.The bench also asked EC to detail steps taken to include names of those whose appeals had been allowed. EC said it was holding meetings with the acting CJ of Calcutta HC and would submit a proposal on expediting disposal.Appearing for some petitioners, advocate Rauf Rahim said people whose names were deleted and whose appeals were pending should not be deprived of ration and benefits under the govt schemes.Advocate Kalyan Bandopadhyay told the bench that in Murshidabad, many constituencies had voter deletions far exceeding winning margin, and alleged a particular community appeared to have been targeted through SIR. SC will hear issue again next week.
Article Summary: Supreme Court was informed Tuesday that against 27-lakh odd deletions from voters’ list because of ‘logical discrepancy’ only seven lakh filed appeals seeking inclusion of their names in electoral rolls. This was new information for SC, which was concerned by pendency of 37 lakh appeals. 19 tribunals in last four months decided only 82,000 appeals.

Article Title: Small island states can serve as labs for innovation and tech: Maldives prez
Article Text:
Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu also announced plans for the country's first Trade Acceleration Zone.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called upon Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to pivot away from being framed solely by climate vulnerability and isolation, while also urging global leaders and private sector partners to view island economies as dynamic "laboratories for innovation".Delivering a keynote statement at the opening ceremony of the Small Island Developing States Global Business Network (SIDS GBN) Forum 2026, Muizzu outlined an economic modernization plan aimed at turning geographic constraints into digital and strategic advantages.With the global dialogue surrounding small island nations focused on their acute climate risk, geographical isolation, and structural economic constraints, Muizzu stressed that vulnerability represents only half the story."For too long, the story of Small Island Developing States has been told primarily through the lens of vulnerability. The other part is our determination. Our scale can become an advantage. SIDS can serve as laboratories for innovation and incubators for ideas, technologies, and solutions,” he said.The president's address focused on the Maldives 2.0 agenda, designed to leverage technology to overcome the traditional barriers of an archipelagic state.Under this strategic initiative, the Maldivian government aims to expand its digital and creative sectors, setting a target for these industries to account for 15 percent of national GDP by 2030.“We have identified the digital economy and digitalisation as central to advancing our economy. Through our Maldives 2.0 agenda, we are working to use digital connectivity to overcome the limitations of geography and scale — making government and financial services more accessible, enabling businesses to operate more efficiently, and connecting Maldivian enterprises and talent to global markets,” said Muizzu.The Maldives is enhancing financial technology accessibility for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Key measures include launching homegrown digital payment platforms such as BML Swipe and expanding international gateway integration through services like PayPal.Muizzu also announced plans for the country's first Trade Acceleration Zone, set to launch by January 1, 2027, to incentivize enterprise development and fast-track commercial growth.While reaffirming the Maldives' commitment to attracting international capital through a modernized foreign investment framework, Muizzu stressed that foreign partnerships must align with national interests. New legal safeguards have been introduced to protect domestic commerce by reserving specific commercial activities strictly for local entities, ensuring economic growth directly benefits Maldivian citizens, he stressed.Muizzu called upon international investors, technology companies, and global financial institutions to establish concrete commercial partnerships with small island states. He reiterated the Maldives' commitment to implementing the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS), urging global stakeholders to bridge the gap between initial innovation and sustainable commercial financing.
Article Summary: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called upon Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to pivot away from being framed solely by climate vulnerability and isolation. He urged global leaders and private sector partners to view island economies as dynamic "laboratories for innovation" MuizzU outlined an economic modernization plan aimed at turning geographic constraints into digital and strategic advantages.

Article Title: 2 killed at NHAI construction sites in J&K
Article Text:
Two separate accidents occurred at NHAI construction sites in Samba and Jammu districts (Representative image)

JAMMU: Two workers, aged 25 and 45, died in two separate accidents at NHAI construction sites in Samba and Jammu districts in J&K on Tuesday.“Gotam Sahu, from Bihar, was engaged in laying the pier of a bridge on the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra project in Samba’s Jakh, when a concrete structure collapsed suddenly, killing him on the spot. Another worker, also from Bihar, suffered injuries,” said NHAI project director Rajiv Kumar.Officials said Sahu’s wife has been given an immediate relief of Rs 5 lakh from the contractor and Rs 5 lakh from the state administration. Another Rs 5 lakh will be credited to her account, they added.In a similar incident, Budhi Singh (45), from Ramban, died after falling from a height at his workplace near Sidhra Tawi Bridge construction site in Jammu on Tuesday, officials said.“He was rushed to Govt Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Jammu, where doctors declared him dead,” an official said.
Article Summary: Two workers, aged 25 and 45, died in two separate accidents at NHAI construction sites in Samba and Jammu districts in J&K on Tuesday. Gotam Sahu, from Bihar, was engaged in laying the pier of a bridge when a concrete structure collapsed suddenly, killing him on the spot. Budhi Singh (45), from Ramban, died after falling from a height at his workplace near Sidhra Tawi Bridge construction site in Jammu.

Article Title: Hydel project shutdown triggers power crisis in J&K
Article Text:
Baglihar stage-I in Ramban district has remained non-operational for a week (Photo for representation)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir is grappling with power shortages and unscheduled outages after key hydroelectric projects, including the 450MW Baglihar stage I and the Salal project, were shut for silt-flushing operations. Baglihar stage-I in Ramban district has remained non-operational for a week, with accumulated silt at its gates delaying restoration work.Officials said desilting work at Baglihar stages I and II and the Salal project began on Aug 18. While Baglihar stage II resumed generation on Aug 22, stage I is yet to restart. Salal is expected to resume operations on Tuesday.The prolonged shutdown has widened the region’s power deficit. Jammu & Kashmir’s peak electricity demand stands at about 2,500MW in summer and 3,000MW in winter. With both Baglihar units largely unavailable for most of the past week, Jammu & Kashmir faced a shortfall of nearly 900MW.Built on the Chenab river, Baglihar stages I and II are among Jammu & Kashmir’s key power sources. Following the disruption, the power department is exploring alternative arrangements to bridge the supply gap.The crisis comes amid criticism of the Omar Abdullah-led govt over rising electricity tariffs. From Sept 1, power consumers in Jammu & Kashmir will face a 6.83% tariff hike.
Article Summary: Baglihar stage-I in Ramban district has remained non-operational for a week. The prolonged shutdown has widened the region’s power deficit. From Sept 1, power consumers in Jammu & Kashmir will face a 6.83% tariff hike.

Article Title: 8 terror suspects held in Kashmir; arms-ammo, posters seized
Article Text:
Six arrests were made in south Kashmir’s Shopian district and two in Pulwama. (File photo)

SRINAGAR: Joint teams of security forces arrested eight terror suspects and seized arms, ammunition, and other incriminating material in separate operations in three Kashmir districts.Six arrests were made in south Kashmir’s Shopian district and two in Pulwama, also in south Kashmir. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmir’s Sopore district, J&K Police said Tuesday, claiming the action had dealt a major blow to terror networks operating in the Union Territory.During a naka check at Shopian’s Heerpora, a joint team of the Army, CRPF and J&K Police intercepted a two-wheeler. Three suspects — Junaid Muzaffar Dar, Aamir Yousaf and Junaid Bashir Dar; all from south Kashmir’s Kulgam district — were arrested after two hand grenades and incriminating posters were recovered from their possession, a police statement said.In a separate operation in Shopian, three terrorist associates — Haris Manzoor, Ashiq Hussain and Arif Ahmad Kumar; all from south Kashmir’s Anantnag district — were arrested by a joint patrolling team of the Army’s 34RR, CRPF, and local police. Security personnel seized a hand grenade, two AK-47 magazines, 20 rounds and incriminating posters from them, the statement said.In Pulwama, a joint team of the Army and police launched a search operation based on intelligence inputs and arrested two terror suspects with a pistol, hand grenade, and ammunition, an Army statement said.In yet another operation in Sopore’s Manzseer area, a combined team of the Army, police and CRPF seized one AK-series rifle, three magazines, four hand grenades, a huge cache of ammunition, and other war-like stores, the Army statement said, adding that further searches were under way.
Article Summary: Six arrests were made in south Kashmir’s Shopian district and two in Pulwama. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmir's Sopore district. Three suspects were arrested after two hand grenades and incriminating posters were recovered from their possession.

Article Title: 'Country is not a dharamshala': Amit Shah sets target for illegal immigration-free India
Article Text:
Amit Shah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday said the Narendra Modi govt has set a goal to make the country illegal immigration-free in a “very short period of time” and, for this purpose, reached out to the border states over the past eight months, sharing with them its document on a quadrangular approach to border security.The policy drawn up by the Centre enlists the border guarding forces, state and district administration, relevant arms of govt of India and local citizens as key stakeholders in securing the borders.Addressing the valedictory session of the national security strategy conference (NSSC) organised by Intelligence Bureau here, Shah reiterated that “this country is not a Dharamshala and only the citizens have the right to live here”. “Infiltrators are a threat of the country’s security, economy and trigger unnatural demographic shifts,” he stated at the event attended by over 850 officials of the Central security agencies and forces, the state/UT police and intelligence agencies.With NSSC focused on anticipating security trends and challenges over the next 15-20 years and devising strategies to avert them, Shah underlined that challenges should be identified and destroyed before they become big."By creating such an ecosystem, we will be able to create a secure, infiltrator-free and narcotics free India,” he told the officers that included both young ones at the cutting-edge level and their seasoned, experienced seniors.Stating that PM Narendra Modi had set the target of making the nation developed by 2047, Shah said the first condition for this would be making its internal security more robust.Commending the state police forces, central agencies and the Central armed police forces (CAPFs) for having eliminated the challenge posed by three hotspots — J&K, Left-wing extremism-hit areas and the north-east — the home minister said that had the past governments visualised these problems before they became acute, the country would not have had to bear the brunt of them for decades.Shah also described the dismantling of the Popular Front of India (PFI) network “in one night” (in multi-state raids of Sept 2022), apart from imposing a ban on it, as “an excellent instance of Centre-state coordination”.The home minister emphasised on the need to take the country’s first anti-terror doctrine — PRAHAAR — from document to practice, to “eradicate terrorism and dismantle the terror ecosystem”. He said the govt has strengthened the anti-fugitive drive, having deported 274 fugitives from different countries between 2019 and 2026. “All the states should aim to bring the fugitives back to face the law here,” he stated.Stating that global instability, lack of energy security, supply chain disruption and increasing radicalisation of cyber misinformation have emerged as the key challenges, Shah insisted that the security policy taken each of these into account and aim to effectively tackle them.With the latest focus of the home minister being to eliminate the drugs menace, Shah sought the cooperation of the states in making the country narcotics-free."Police of all states should implement the Narcotics Control Vision Document 2026-2029 on the ground to protect the new generation and work on three D's ‘detect, disrupt and destroy’ for "a drug-free India,” he stated.Shah also asked the officers to used the integrated data bank of CCTNS, ICJS, Natgrid and NAFIS to develop actionable intelligence through data integration, analysis and identification of modus operandi through AI, so that future challenges can be prevented.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah said the Narendra Modi govt has set a goal to make the country illegal immigration-free in a ‘very short period of time’ Shah reiterated that “this country is not a Dharamshala and only the citizens have the right to live here’
